clue.text: It takes the shine off a Minack performance

definitions.text: It takes the shine off a Minack performance

parts.words: It takes the shine off a Minack performance
parts.note: the Minack is an open-air theatre on a Cornish clifftop, so what spoils a show there is a dull, cloudy heaven that blots out the sun

explanation.surface: Something that dims the glamour of a show at the famous Cornish cliff theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the shine off' sounds like a figure of speech for spoiling, but here it is literal: at an open-air venue, cloud cover blocks the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloud-covered heaven literally removes the sunshine from an outdoor theatre performance.

clue.text: Customs may demand to do it, but it's hard to defend

definitions.text: Customs may demand to do it
definitions.meaning: officers at a border may ask you to unfasten your luggage for inspection and then fasten it again
a legal matter so clear-cut that the defence has almost no chance

explanation.surface: Border officials' demands set against a lawyer's hopeless brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally as three actions on a suitcase; the second is the idiom for a straightforward legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a lawsuit whose outcome is obvious, so the defending side can hardly contest it.

clue.text: Acclaim the French in shock treatment

indicators.note: the French article is placed inside the abbreviation for the therapy

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric shock treatment
la is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Praise for the French within electric therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliant success or acclaim, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Where to put a bit of coin — under the boiler?

indicators.note: just a small piece, the opening letter, is taken from the word coin

parts.note: an ash box is the receptacle beneath an old coal-fired boiler's firebox that catches the ash

explanation.surface: A household question about where to stash loose change, perhaps beneath the boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hiding money under a boiler; in fact 'under the boiler' describes the ash box of an old coal-fired boiler. The definition 'Where to put' reaches through the whole clue to coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash box is a container where one puts money for safekeeping.

clue.text: Drink with soldiers — you can't beat it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A drink with the troops, and nothing can top it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supreme is the very best, so nothing can surpass or beat it.

clue.text: Animal's taken up by little sibling — that's the general idea

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pony's, with the possessive giving the S
sis is a short, familiar word for sister

explanation.surface: A child's younger sister picks up a pet, and that's roughly the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief summary giving the overall gist of something.

clue.text: Uncertain consequences of joining MI5?

definitions.meaning: the phrase expresses that the outcome is not predictable
MI5 is the British security service, and its officers are sworn to secrecy, so they may not tell anyone anything

explanation.surface: What follows if you sign up for British intelligence is anyone's guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: someone in the security service is forbidden to tell. MI5 is the UK's domestic intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means the outcome is unpredictable, matching a sense of doubt or uncertainty.

clue.text: Ring tone? No, try again

parts.note: read as a telephone noise, it is the beeping heard when a line is busy, telling the caller to ring later; 'Ring' also hints at a betrothal band

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a phone ringtone rejects one and tries another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring tone' suggests a mobile phone jingle, but it is the tone you get on ringing a busy line, which tells you to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: The busy tone on a telephone line tells the caller the number is in use and to call later.

clue.text: Show strong disapproval as the treble disastrously sang up first

indicators.note: the reversed singing word is placed at the front
in a down clue, up means reading the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something done disastrously is wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: treble means three times, so the word 'the' is written out thrice

explanation.surface: A boy soprano sings badly and earns a scowl of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treble' looks like a choirboy singing, but it means three times over; 'disastrously' is the anagram signal, 'up' the reversal in a down clue, and 'first' places that reversed piece at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding one's teeth is a classic biblical image of anger or frustrated displeasure.

clue.text: Boy born and died before getting jabs

indicators.note: born and died come ahead of the boy in the answer

parts.note: née marks a maiden name, meaning born
Les is a man's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: A boy's whole life summed up before his vaccinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the sharp instruments of injections, so they stand for jabs.

clue.text: Writer in spirit acceptable to publisher

parts.note: a pen is something to write with

indicators.note: the letter for acceptable goes inside the spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: An author with the right spirit wins over a publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class or acceptable is an old British convention from the 'U and non-U' debate on class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin is a well-known British paperback publishing house.

clue.text: Versatile girl with ability to swallow a pint

indicators.note: the girl and the ability take the pint inside them, as if drinking it

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
able, having the ability, stands for ability here
pt is the abbreviation for a pint

explanation.surface: A capable girl who can down a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: The pint goes between the girl and the ability word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile adjusts readily to new circumstances, which is a synonym of adaptable.

clue.text: Media report lack of ease in noble lady

indicators.note: the letters are missing from the noble lady

parts.note: a peeress is a woman holding a peerage

indicators.note: the word ease is heard, and spoken it is the same as the plural of the letter E

parts.note: said, it sounds like 'E's', two letter Es

explanation.surface: Newspapers report on a titled woman who is ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' tells you to hear 'ease' as E's, two Es; 'lack of' takes those two Es out of PEERESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is a collective term for newspapers and journalists, the news media.

clue.text: Lad in a whirl

definitions.meaning: A boy's name, short for Edward
a swirling current of water or air

explanation.surface: A boy in a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular swirl of water or air, as well as a boy's name.

clue.text: Soldiers follow one in specialist trial

indicators.note: the one and soldiers sit inside the specialist

parts.note: an expert is a specialist

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops come after a single expert in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a scientific test or trial.

clue.text: Militant believer's game to invest in sacred operation

indicators.note: the game is put inside, as if besieging or clothing it
the letters of sacred are put through an operation, being worked on and rearranged

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A zealot's sport is to put money into a holy enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' is the anagram signal and 'to invest in' the container signal; 'invest' looks financial but here has its old sense of besieging or surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader fought for the faith in holy wars, so a militant believer.

clue.text: Dozen chairs, one removed, dancing with playfulness

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move around into a new order
the one letter is taken away from chairs

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Twelve chairs, minus one, joining a merry dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes I (one) out of CHAIRS, leaving CHARS; 'dancing' rearranges DOZEN and CHARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzando is a musical direction meaning to be played in a playful, jesting manner.

clue.text: Tessa, say, intimate before lunch

annotationWithheld.why: Tessa, say, intimate before lunch: CRONY (intimate) inside AM (before lunch), but no word signals the insertion; 'before lunch' would have to give AM and be the container indicator at once

clue.text: Doctor following planner

parts.note: after means following

explanation.surface: A doctor following a planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A drafter draws up plans or drafts, so is a planner.

clue.text: 100 are about enough space for several houses

indicators.note: the word are goes round the hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred ares give roughly room for a few homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the metric land unit: 100 ares is a hectare. Here 'are' is just the word, wrapped round C.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, enough to build a handful of houses on.

clue.text: Openings for a rich man

definitions.meaning: Bill ..., the Microsoft founder, is one of the world's richest people

explanation.surface: Doorways for a wealthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are openings in walls, and Bill Gates is a famously wealthy man.

clue.text: Reorganise back row

parts.note: rear means back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Shuffle the seats at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put things in a different order, to reorganise.

clue.text: Floral tribute reported for old radio chief

indicators.note: the floral tribute is heard rather than seen, so its sound gives the name

parts.note: a wreath is a ring of flowers laid as a tribute

explanation.surface: Flowers mentioned for a former broadcasting boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Reith was the first director-general of the BBC, which began as a radio broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded and led the BBC in its early radio days.

clue.text: Hell is for a rotten fellow

parts.note: bad means rotten
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Hell is meant for a wicked man.
explanation.walkthrough: Abaddon is a Biblical and Miltonic name for the abyss or Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaddon is a poetic, Biblical name for the bottomless pit of Hell.

clue.text: Intent to get shot of useless weaponry

annotationWithheld.why: Intent to get shot of useless weaponry: RID inside TENT, but the one word 'Intent' gives both the insertion indicator (in) and the container (TENT), doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Intent to get shot of useless weaponry

clue.text: Norfolk noble wounds old prince

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
mars means damages or wounds
Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Prince Henry, later Henry V

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from Norfolk injures a former prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dukes of Norfolk have held this office hereditarily since 1672, so 'Norfolk' alone defines it. Norfolk is an English county, here a duke's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary office of England's ceremonial officer belongs to the Duke of Norfolk, so the title stands for him.
